## <small>2.7.1 (2026-11-24)</small>

### Summary

Version 2.7.1 expands the bundled managed skills that guide day-to-day work. A new vv-verification skill adds one language-agnostic decision workflow with six on-demand references covering strategy, oracles, evidence, formal methods, maintenance, and bootstrapping a project verification stack, while vv-spec and vv-plan now ask for verification intent inside their existing fields so plans name the property and oracle behind each criterion. Two new writing skills, vv-write-for-humans for reader-facing prose and vv-write-for-agents for agent-executed instructions, are hardened with clearer trigger wording and tighter content, banned-token, and volume gates so they install predictably. The design-guidance skill is renamed from vv-design-principles to vv-ui-design-principles, so anyone invoking the old name should switch to the new one. Install and sync test expectations are now derived from the skill registry, keeping counts accurate as skills are added, and the guidance docs gained a rule against piping gate commands without pipefail plus a pinned reviewer prompt shape.

## 2.7.0 (2026-11-24)

### Summary

Version 2.7.0 adds the vv-design-principles managed skill, giving agents a build-and-audit design process for web and app UI: it plans design tokens before writing code, enforces a measurable quality floor, runs a subtractive audit against a catalog of generic design tells, and anchors decisions in a project DESIGN.md design-system file, with the tell catalog, quality-floor numbers, and DESIGN.md contract loaded on demand from three bundled references. The skill is registered in the managed-skill list so vvoc install and sync ship it and doctor can report drift, and it is documented in the README as an additive companion to existing design skills. The release also tightens DESIGN.md discovery so it stays within the current package, reorganizes and clarifies several catalog entries for more accurate guidance, and improves the quality-floor verification steps to distinguish what was actually checked from what still needs confirmation.

## <small>2.6.1 (2026-11-22)</small>

### Summary

Version 2.6.1 fixes runtime session handling so that session-created reconciliation, family-settings resolution and birth, and auxiliary work only act on sessions whose location directory matches the plugin runtime. Role application is now location-owned, family roots keep their native model, and creation reconciliation compares the freshly read session model instead of the creation event. This prevents cross-location interference and keeps sessions outside the runtime's location read-only, which matters for users running multiple locations who need predictable model selection and isolation between them; foreign-location and family-root coverage was added to lock in the behavior.

* fix(runtime): isolate session mutation to the owning location ([613510f](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/613510f))

## 2.6.0 (2026-11-10)

### Summary

Version 2.6.0 fixes a data-corruption bug in the str_replace_editor tool used by the Hashline Edit plugin. Concurrent edits to the same file could previously collide and leave contents corrupted; the plugin now serializes complete read, check, write, and cache cycles per canonical target across sessions in one process, and publishes byte-verified staged UTF-8 writes atomically while preserving file mode and symlinks. As a result, users and agents can safely edit the same files from multiple sessions without producing mangled or truncated content, and failed or cancelled operations recover cleanly instead of leaving stale output behind.

* fix(editor): prevent concurrent str_replace_editor corruption ([a991c13](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/a991c13))

## 2.5.0 (2026-11-08)

### Summary

Version 2.5.0 replaces the previous family snapshot and rebind machinery with session-owned settings stored in native session metadata: the resolved roles, orchestration profile, and plugin toggles of the effective configuration are recorded once for a session family's root and resolved through lineage for every member, while read-modify-write updates preserve unrelated metadata. Settings are now changed explicitly through the new `vvoc session set --session <id>` command (preset, profile, role, plugin toggle, or pull-defaults) and the TUI `/vv-settings` command, so only the named family changes; the `--force` and `--session` rebind flags on preset, role, and plugin commands and the `/vv-rebind` command are removed, and all native plugins read their policy through the shared settings service instead of the deleted snapshot configFor/accept pair. Controller guidance was also consolidated into the bundled seven-section template delivered exactly once by system-context-injection without duplicate injection, with other primary agents receiving shared guidance fragments. Documentation, GRACE projections, the real-host harness cases, and integration tests were synchronized for session settings, including isolated workflow test persistence and stability of recorded settings across configuration changes and host restarts.

issues.title: workflow: revertInFlightDelegatedLaunches is dead code — delegated attempts orphaned by a host crash stay in_flight forever (ATTEMPT_IN_FLIGHT, no recover path)
runtime: family-snapshot admission rejects its own first-work model switch — bare sessions whose creation model differs from roles.default die on first dispatch (SnapshotAdmissionError, 2.4.0)
workflow: a checkpoint reviewer launch that dies at transport permanently binds the generation slot (ALREADY_LAUNCHED deadlock, no recover path)
vv-plan/vv-spec: XML-authoring hazards undocumented; the lint accepts malformed XML that a strict parser rejects; self-review lacks a contract-fidelity check
